A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaMo work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison; v2 retains the earlier material and adds supplementary analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, motion-generation and captioning results, ablations, latency measurements, and a 14-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds caption-distribution analysis and qualitative reconstruction comparisons in Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: The MoT architecture, frozen language parameters, continuous causal tokenizer, flow-matching head, exit head and training procedure are unchanged. Section 11's sigma-causal TAE refers to the tokenizer already described in v1, not a new component.

E1.justification: The training mixture, HumanML3D evaluation, MotionMillion-Eval prompts, internal test split and language-task coverage remain unchanged. The new appendix analyses examine corpus semantics and existing codec reconstruction without introducing a distinct task, domain or input condition.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged. MotionMillion's FSQ tokenizer, illustrated in v2 Figure 8, was already evaluated against LLaMo's tokenizer in v1 Table 2; the new figure extends that reconstruction comparison qualitatively.

E3.justification: The added dataset analysis introduces Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B encoding, t-SNE projection, independent K-means clustering and density-based subsampling. Figure 7 labels n=50,000 and K=50. Existing benchmark protocols and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a semantic-distribution analysis of MotionMillion versus internal captions in Figure 7 and a qualitative tokenizer reconstruction comparison in Section 11/Figure 8. Existing architecture, tokenizer-variance and training-stage ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports additional repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests relative to the other. The 14-participant user study and its reporting practice are unchanged; Figure 7's sample count describes the new analysis, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figures 7–8 add qualitative findings about caption-distribution differences and reconstruction fidelity. Existing numerical results in Tables 2–7 and Figures 5–6 are unchanged; the additions do not establish a performance improvement over v1's model.

T1.justification: The motion representation, latent construction, architecture equations and training objectives remain unchanged. The added embedding visualization and reconstruction discussion introduce no mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified motion understanding and generation, preserved language capability, continuous autoregressive tokens and real-time streaming. The added homepage sentence changes access information, not these claims.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's criticism of MotionMillion caption hallucinations, v2 interprets Figure 7 as indicating semantic redundancy and narrower coverage than its internal dataset. The reconstruction discussion reinforces an existing explanation; the stated model limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new analysis's embedding model, encoding prompt, clustering and visualization procedure, and adds a project-homepage pointer. Existing implementation, hardware and inference details are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Works section remain unchanged, but the new dataset comparison adds a specific positioning argument: the internal corpus provides broader, less redundant motion semantics than MotionMillion.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Dataset Comparison passage within Section 10, Section 11 on auto-encoder comparison, acknowledgments and a homepage sentence. The existing prose and overall section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel t-SNE Figure 7, reconstruction Figure 8 and a boxed encoding prompt, with localized text reflow. Existing Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7 retain their displays and content.

improvement.justification: v1 quantified reconstruction quality but lacked the matched ground-truth/reconstruction illustration now supplied by Figure 8, making the reported errors easier to inspect. Figure 7 and its documented encoding procedure add useful dataset analysis, although the broad semantic-diversity interpretation has only qualitative support from 2D plots. These are limited evidential and explanatory gains; the core method and quantitative validation remain unchanged.
